title: Establish per-token provenance chain to prevent orphaned billing and enable safe retroactive corrections
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description: Problem: We still encounter orphaned or misattributed token charges when streaming sessions are multiplexed, when frames are de-duplicated after retries, or when backfilled/compacted ledgers are applied. Existing token tallies are often just aggregate counters per session; they lack a minimal provenance chain tying each credited token to the originating request, session boundary, API key, model variant, and the staging kernel/quantization path. Without this, retroactive corrections (backfills, reconciliations after a dedupe, or model-switch prorations) are risky and can lead to customer over/under-billing or inconsistent quotas.\n\nGoal: Add a compact, immutable per-token provenance record that travels through the metering pipeline (ingest -> batching -> rpc -> runtime -> billing), enabling deterministically idempotent reconciliation and safe retroactive corrections. The design must be low-overhead (minimal per-token metadata), compatible with current streaming semantics (partial frames, resume tokens, midstream model fallbacks), and support efficient compaction for long-lived sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Every token credited in the ledger includes a provenance tuple: root_request_id, session_id, client_api_key_hash, model_variant, encoding_version, kernel_id, and attribution_timestamp (ISO8601).
Replay and dedupe tests show idempotent billing: replaying identical frames with the same root_request_id does not double-charge (>= 5 automated test scenarios).
Compaction job reduces token provenance storage to <2x current storage after 30 days while preserving ability to retroactively correct last-7-day charges.
Rollout step toggles: feature flag enables provenance recording and a read-path fallback to previous aggregate method for 24h validation window.
Metrics: fraction of tokens with provenance == 100% after rollout; reconciliation error rate < 0.01% in Canary; end-to-end latency impact < 0.5ms P50.
steps_taken: 2026-02-22: Spike implemented a prototype provenance tuple carried as compact binary header in the streaming frame. Microbenchmarked overhead with continuous batching: ~0.12ms per request and +6% payload. (spike/branch: spike/eng/prov-compact)
2026-02-27: Schema review with Data and Billing; removed full API key from tuple and replaced with salted hash to avoid PII in the ledger. Decision recorded in design doc.

2026-03-03: Implemented idempotency check at the credit-aggregator: use root_request_id + frame_sequence + model_variant as dedupe key. Leak test uncovered race when aggregator shard boundary changed during autoscale.
2026-03-07: Added deterministic shard routing for provenance dedupe keys and a fast-fail path if shard mapping is stale; unit tests added.

2026-03-09: End-to-end Canary run started in us-west-2 on a small tenant cohort (10 customers). Observed one reconciliation divergence due to time-synchronization skew between runtime and billing worker — mitigation: switch to monotonic sequence numbers for local attribution time and store UTC timestamp for audit only.
decision_log: Keep provenance tuple compact: avoid storing full prompt/response text. Store only references (request_digest) to allow later on-demand retrieval from retention store.
Use salted SHA256 of API key (server-side salt rotated monthly) to identify clients without exposing key material to downstream systems.
Perform dedupe at the final credit-aggregator so upstream components can remain stateless for performance, but ensure dedupe-key routing determinism to avoid split-brain credits.
risks_and_mitigations: Storage growth: provenance adds metadata per token. Mitigation: compaction policy that collapses contiguous tokens from the same root_request_id into run-length entries after 7 days.
Performance regression: extra header increases serialization cost. Mitigation: use binary-compact encoding and add a feature flag to disable provenance for low-value test tenants.
Privacy/compliance: API key hashing must meet audit requirements. Mitigation: implementation reviewed by Security and Compliance; server-side salt and KMS-protected rotation included.
Cross-shard race on dedupe: Mitigation: introduce mapping version pinning during shard rebalance and a transient reconciliation buffer to catch late-arriving frames.
test_plan: Unit tests for provenance tuple encode/decode and compact run-length compaction.
Integration tests: streaming session with intermittent reconnects, duplicate frames, midstream model fallback, and mixed batching windows.
Chaos tests: kill aggregator shard and verify no double-charges during rebalance.
Backfill simulation: run reconciliation job across synthetic historical data and assert corrections match expected deltas across 10k sessions.
Load test: Canary at 10% traffic on us-west-2 for 72h measuring latency and reconciliation metrics.
next_steps: Finish compaction worker implementation and add a stonewall rollback that rehydrates per-token details for disputed charges.
Address monotonic timestamping: switch local attribution_time to sequence numbers and store UTC only for audit logs.
Create migration plan for existing 30-day ledger to backfill provenance for the last 7 days using sampling heuristics.
Open PR for aggregator deterministic routing: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/17280
Schedule cross-team review with Billing, Data, and Security on 2026-03-12 to sign off on canary gating criteria.
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids storing prompt/response bodies in the ledger to keep costs and PII lower; disputes will escalate to a separate tranche that fetches traces from the retention store.
If the compaction policy proves lossy for certain dispute classes, we will extend retention selectively for affected customers under SLA.
